audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line is the tracked ability in every string of both layers, and the only advice attached to it is 'dodge it' or 'trade when it is down'. The clause that actually answers it is never mentioned, and Trundle's own Pillar of Ice is described only as a way to deny his retreat.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together. Colliding with TERRAIN pulls Nautilus towards it.' Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain. So a pillar placed between the two of them turns his engage into a self-pull onto the wall — the hook resolves on the pillar and Trundle is not moved at all. That converts Pillar from a retreat-denial tool into the direct counter to the one ability the whole entry is organised around, and no string in either layer says it.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line that collides with terrain pulls Nautilus to the terrain instead. Pillar of Ice is terrain — a pillar between you answers the hook outright.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json (Q Dredge Line, terrain flag, cd 14/13/12/11/10, range 1150)
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, impassable terrain)

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow is described as rooting on every auto-attack in four separate strings: mid says 'every auto he lands roots you briefly', whys[1] says 'the passive root sticks to you every auto', spikes[0] says 'the passive root on every auto', and wants.foe[1] says 'Apply the passive root through consecutive autos to slow your attack speed window'.
audit.why: Riot: 'Nautilus' FIRST Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly.' It is one root per target as the engagement opens, not a chain riding every attack. The difference decides how Trundle plays the trade: the entry's version says extended trades are unplayable because he is permanently rooted, when actually the root is a one-time tax at the start and the extended trade — which is Trundle's whole win condition — is available once it has been paid. wants.foe[1] also calls the root a slow on the attack-speed window; a root is neither.
audit.corrected: Staggering Blow roots on his FIRST attack against you, not on every one. Pay it at the start of the trade, then the extended fight is still yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown or range appears anywhere in either layer. mid says 'treat his hook cooldown as the lane timer' without ever giving the timer. Titan's Wrath is named only once, as 'his W shield' in dontsFull[2].t, and never described.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10 at 1150 range against Chomp's 300, which is both the window and the reason the walk-up is the problem. Riptide is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5 — twice per hook, which is why the slow feels constant. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield during which his attacks apply damage over time to Trundle and everything around him, so 'extend into his W shield' is a warning with a number attached. And Depth Charge is 120/100/80, exactly Subjugate's timer, so the level-6 stage is a mirrored window rather than one he simply owns.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line 14s at rank 1 from 1150. Riptide 7s at rank 1. Titan's Wrath a flat 12s. Depth Charge 120/100/80 — the same as Subjugate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json (Q cd 14/13/12/11/10 range 1150; W cd 12; E cd 7/6.5/6/5.5/5; R cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: late says to 'keep Pillar of Ice as your escape from Depth Charge', and whys[4] treats Pillar as the answer to the ultimate.
audit.why: Depth Charge 'fires a shockwave into the earth that chases an opponent' and rips up the ground as it travels. Nothing in Riot's text suggests a terrain wall interacts with it, and it tracks the target rather than travelling a fixed line, so holding a 21-second cooldown as an escape from it is a bad trade. Pillar has a verified job in this matchup — collapsing his hook — and spending it on the ultimate means it is down when the hook comes.
audit.corrected: Spend Pillar of Ice on Dredge Line, which it genuinely answers, rather than saving it for Depth Charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Trundle five of seven stages (Trundle, Trundle, Trundle, Skill, Trundle, Trundle, Skill) while the prose says the opposite at four of them. mid opens 'From level 2 onward Nautilus controls the terms of the fight'; whys[1] says 'he controls the tempo from here'; whys[3] says 'you are reactively waiting for the cooldown window'; whys[5] says 'he remains firmly in control of the pace of the lane'.
audit.why: The packet has this at 50.78% over 642 games — the largest sample in the slice and almost exactly even — so a chart handing Trundle five stages is not supportable, and it is directly contradicted by the entry's own reasoning at Levels 2, 3, 6 and first item. With the hook-versus-Pillar interaction stated, Level 3 onward is genuinely contestable rather than lost, but 'Trundle' is the wrong label at the stages where the whys describe him reacting.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill; Levels 2 to first item Nautilus or Skill, matching the whys; two-plus items Skill. win[1], win[2], win[4] and win[5] should not read Trundle.

edits.before: At level 1 both kits are roughly equivalent in threat — your Chomp does bite his AD and the first auto-trade is in your favor, but Nautilus's passive root procs on his first auto back, meaning you rarely get a free exchange. Play footsies along the wave and take the Chomp proc whenever he steps for a last-hit, but do not walk into a position where he can land Dredge Line from fog or off an angle. His hook range at level 1 is dangerous the moment he hits level 2 and you should track when he hits it first. Keep the wave slightly pushed toward your side — forcing him to walk up exposes him to your Q bites, and every proc of King's Tribute off dying minions chips away at the HP gap.
edits.after: At level 1 both kits are close — Chomp saps his AD and the first auto-trade favours you, but Staggering Blow roots you on his first attack back, so the opener is never free. Play footsies along the wave and take the Chomp whenever he steps for a last-hit, but stay off any angle where Dredge Line reaches: it is 1150 range against your 300, on 14s at rank 1. Bank one fact for later — a hook that collides with terrain pulls Nautilus to the terrain instead, and Pillar of Ice is terrain. Keep the wave slightly to your side; making him walk up exposes him to the bite, and every King's Tribute proc chips the HP gap back.

edits.before: From level 2 onward Nautilus controls the terms of the fight: his hook dictates when he engages, and every auto he lands roots you briefly, interrupting your Frozen Domain pathing and denying the full AD-steal stack. The correct response is to treat his hook cooldown as the lane timer — when Dredge Line is down, drop Frozen Domain immediately, Chomp him twice, and Pillar behind him so he cannot retreat. When his hook is up, give him nothing and last-hit from range. At level 6 his Depth Charge (R) means a straight all-in is risky unless you have a sizable HP advantage; Subjugate is still potent because draining a tank's armor and MR is valuable, but you need to pop R early and let the drained stats do the work through the rest of the fight rather than trading freely into his full kit on equal HP.
edits.after: From level 2 Nautilus dictates terms: Dredge Line decides when the fight happens from 1150 range, and Staggering Blow roots you on his first attack of each engagement — once, as it opens, not on every auto. Treat the hook as the lane timer: it is 14s at rank 1, so when it is spent, drop Frozen Domain, Chomp twice, and Pillar behind him. When it is up, give nothing and last-hit from range. And know the real counter — a Dredge Line that collides with terrain pulls Nautilus to the terrain instead of pulling you, and Pillar of Ice creates terrain, so a pillar between you answers the hook rather than merely walling his exit. At 6 Depth Charge is 120/100/80, exactly Subjugate's timer; cast R early so the doubled theft covers the whole exchange, and remember Riptide comes back every 7s.

edits.before: Late game the matchup flips back toward parity: Subjugate into a fully stacked Nautilus is one of the most impactful abilities in the game because you are literally converting his Heartsteel HP-based resistances into your own, and in 5v5 he is exactly the kind of frontline tank your R was designed for. The problem is getting there — if Nautilus snowballed lane, his item lead means his hook can one-shot combo you before R does enough work. Play for the side lane, keep Pillar of Ice as your escape from Depth Charge, and in team fights R the first tank who steps up and let your team collapse. You do not beat him cleanly in a solo duel at this stage without Subjugate up and Frozen Domain active simultaneously.
edits.after: Late the matchup returns to parity: Subjugate into a fully stacked Nautilus is among the most impactful casts in the game, because it takes a percentage of the Health, Armor and MR his tank build piles up and doubles the theft over four seconds. In 5v5 he is exactly the frontliner your R exists for. The problem is arriving there — a Nautilus with an item lead hooks from 1150 and chains Riptide's 7s into Depth Charge before the theft does its work. Play the side lane, spend Pillar of Ice on the hook it genuinely answers rather than saving it for his ultimate, and in fights R the first tank who steps up. Depth Charge and Subjugate are both 120/100/80, so the two timers reset together.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: Dredge Line 'colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it', and Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain. A pillar placed between them turns his engage into a self-pull onto the wall — Trundle is not moved at all. Every string in both layers organises the matchup around the hook and none of them mentions that Trundle carries a direct answer to it; Pillar was described only as retreat denial. This also changes where the 21-second cooldown should be spent, which is why I moved it off Depth Charge. CORRECTED: Staggering Blow described as rooting on every auto-attack in four strings. Riot says it is his FIRST attack against a target. That is a one-time tax as the trade opens, not a chain — which matters because the entry used the false version to argue Trundle can never run an extended trade, and the extended trade is his entire win condition. ADDED NUMBERS: Dredge Line 14s at rank 1 from 1150 against Chomp's 300, Riptide 7s at rank 1 (twice per hook, which is why the slow feels constant), Titan's Wrath a flat 12s shield whose damage ticks on you while it holds, and Depth Charge 120/100/80 — exactly Subjugate's timer, so level 6 is a shared window rather than his. Titan's Wrath appeared only as the phrase 'his W shield' with nothing attached. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Depth Charge interacts with terrain at all. Riot describes a shockwave that travels through the earth and chases the target, so I removed the instruction to hold Pillar as an escape from it rather than asserting that terrain does or does not stop it — the kit files' needsResearch blocks are empty. NOT EDITED (enum): the chart gives Trundle five of seven stages in the largest-sample lane in the slice (50.78% over 642 games) while mid, whys[1], whys[3] and whys[5] all say Nautilus controls the tempo at those exact stages. win[1], win[2], win[4] and win[5] should not read Trundle; I raised it as a question rather than rewriting four values on prose alone.
